title: Reserved Top Level DNS Names
summary: Sets aside a few top-level domain names such as test, example, invalid and localhost for testing and documentation, and reserves example.com, example.net and example.org as second-level names. Using them avoids clashes with real websites.

eli5.summary: When a teacher writes a sample address on a board, she uses a pretend one so no real house gets mail. These reserved names are the pretend addresses of the Internet.

subtitle: Four top level domain names set aside so tests and examples never collide with real names.

tldr.problem: Sites and documents invent top level domains for tests and examples, which can later clash with real TLDs or let test code reach the real DNS.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2606 reserves .test, .example, .invalid and .localhost, and lists example.com, example.net and example.org as reserved second level examples.
tldr.outcome: IANA agreed to the four reservations. The RFC is updated by RFC 6761.

today: RFC 2606 is a Best Current Practice that is updated by RFC 6761.

sections.title: The Problem with Made-Up Names
sections.content:
The DNS defines a tree of names starting with the root, ., with top level domains such as .com and .us directly below.

A site may set up unused local TLDs for testing, and these may later come into actual use globally, so local tests could thwart access to real data. Test or example code may also reference a real TLD and later escape its testbed or actually run on the Internet.
sections.eli5: If you invent a pretend town name for a game and a real town gets that name, your game maps get confusing.

sections.title: The Four Reserved TLDs
sections.content:
RFC 2606 reserves four names:

  • .test is recommended for testing current or new DNS related code.
  • .example is recommended for documentation or as examples.
  • .invalid is for online construction of names that are sure to be invalid and obviously so at a glance.
  • .localhost has traditionally been defined in host DNS implementations with an A record pointing to the loop back IP address, and is reserved for that use.
sections.eli5: There are four pretend names: one for tests, one for examples, one for obviously wrong names, and one meaning 'this very computer'.

sections.title: Reserved Second Level Names
sections.content: IANA also has example.com, example.net and example.org reserved for use as examples.
sections.eli5: Three safe pretend addresses are also kept for use in examples.

sections.title: IANA and Security Considerations
sections.content: IANA has agreed to the four top level reservations. The security section says confusion and conflict arise when real or future TLDs are used for testing or examples, and that test software can escape and run against the global DNS. Reserving these names minimizes the problem.
sections.eli5: Keeping pretend names separate stops practice from spilling into real life.
